title: New Testament — Laws, Commands, and Instructions
content:
New Testament — Laws, Commands, and Instructions

All Laws, Commands, and Instructions · Old Testament · New Testament books · Existing study index

This is the New Testament section of the single Bible-wide Laws, Commands, and Instructions study. Its scope is all 27 books, from Matthew through Revelation: the commands and instruction of Jesus, apostolic teaching, directions to particular people and churches, and the calls to faithfulness in Revelation.

Available now: the existing 105 Christ studies and 124 apostolic teachings are gathered below by the book of their primary Scripture citation. Four selected Revelation records are also linked. These are inherited study records, not a complete or deduplicated count of individual New Testament commands. Some studies concern doctrine or promises; their instructional content still needs separate review.

Open a book to see its current study records and follow each Scripture link to Saints Translation. Parallel passages and fuller commentary remain on the original linked study. A book with no record in this primary-citation grouping still belongs in the catalogue; it has not been certified as containing no instructions.

Browse every New Testament book

Topics and application

Read across both Testaments by topic: knowing, loving and obeying God; love, mercy and forgiveness; prayer, fasting and giving; marriage and family; holiness and truthfulness; justice and authority; church life, service and mission; and trust and watchfulness. The Torah topic sections remain the earlier part of this developing cross-Testament arrangement.

The shared application categories are Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged and Everlasting, with historical scope and uncertainty recorded separately. These are editorial assessments supported by passages, not labels added to Scripture. New Testament instructions with no established Old Testament counterpart are retained in their own right; they are not forced into a continuity category. Duties of a particular role or church remain distinct from duties for all believers.

This page reorganizes existing research and does not assign new application judgments. Read the classification definitions and the historical and review categories.

What remains to complete the New Testament catalogue

Read every chapter and identify separate duties, prohibitions, counsel and commissions; record speaker, recipient and setting; distinguish commands from descriptions, promises, prayers and rejected orders; connect repeated and parallel teaching without erasing differences; and support each application classification from Scripture. Book coverage is tracked separately from a claim that every instruction has been found.
